anchor: despite or in spite of + NP or V-ing

anchor: although with an explicit subject after a reduction

target_pattern: Even if + subject + verb, main clause

anchor: as long as or so long as + finite clause

anchor: provided or providing that + finite clause

target_pattern: main clause + in case + subject + verb

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced condition with omitted subject and be

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced condition with omitted subject and be

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced condition
confusables: if + finite passive clause; unless + past participle clause

target_pattern: Unless otherwise stated / Unless stated otherwise
meaning_or_distinction: uses a conventional passive exception formula meaning unless another rule or instruction says otherwise

meaning_or_distinction: locates the main event at the time of another event

meaning_or_distinction: orders the main event later than another full event
evidence_note: Finite alternative has its own expressed subject.

target_pattern: Before or After + V-ing, main clause

meaning_or_distinction: states that one event follows as soon as a condition/event is complete

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced passive time/condition clause

target_pattern: main clause + as soon as + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: marks the earliest time at which the main action follows
confusables: once + finite clause; when + finite clause

anchor: future time clauses use present forms
connector_or_marker: when; after; before; until; once; as soon as

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced time clause with a recoverable shared subject

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced time clause

target_pattern: When + adjective or prepositional phrase, main clause

target_pattern: main clause + so that + subject + modal or appropriate finite verb

target_pattern: main clause + in order that + subject + modal or appropriate finite verb

anchor: as if versus informal like + finite clause
target_pattern: main clause + as if/like + subject + verb

target_pattern: main clause + as though + subject + verb

anchor: modal remoteness after as if or as though

anchor: in contrast to or with + NP

target_pattern: Contrary to + expectation or claim, main clause

target_pattern: In case of + event or emergency, instruction

target_pattern: by the time + subject + verb, main clause

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced concession whose affected understood subject is the main-clause subject

target_pattern: Though + role noun phrase, main clause

meaning_or_distinction: uses an adjective state as a reduced while-clause with omitted subject and be

meaning_or_distinction: uses an idiomatic prepositional state as a reduced while-clause

target_pattern: If + role noun phrase, main clause

evidence_note: The understood V-ing subject must be the main-clause subject.

meaning_or_distinction: adds a simultaneous or closely following action by the same subject
confusables: and + finite clause; result V-ing clause
evidence_note: Use comma and context to prevent a result reading when sequence is intended.

meaning_or_distinction: adds a natural result or consequence of the main event
evidence_note: The result must follow plausibly from the whole preceding clause.

target_pattern: Knowing or Understanding + clause content, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: states a reason known by the main-clause subject
confusables: because + finite clause; as + finite clause
evidence_note: Use mental-state participles with a clearly shared experiencer.

meaning_or_distinction: negates the non-finite action or state while preserving the shared subject
confusables: without + V-ing; because not + finite clause
evidence_note: Without + V-ing is a preposition pattern and remains outside this module.

meaning_or_distinction: marks an action completed before the main-clause event
evidence_note: Required boundary: Having completed the audit, ... belongs here.

target_pattern: Not having + past participle, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: marks an earlier action or experience that did not occur
confusables: because not + finite clause; without + V-ing
evidence_note: Keep tense relation explicit in the context.

target_pattern: Having been + past participle, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: marks that the main-clause subject had already received or undergone the passive action before the main event
notes: The affected understood subject must be the main-clause subject; include a non-dangling matched example.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive participial clause whose understood subject is the main-clause subject
evidence_note: Use e.g. Designed for small teams, the tool is easy to deploy.

meaning_or_distinction: adds a passive state or accompanying characterization of the main-clause subject
confusables: finite passive clause; noun reduced relative
evidence_note: Ensure the postposed phrase modifies the clause subject, not a nearby noun accidentally.

meaning_or_distinction: states an accepted fact or condition as the basis for a conclusion
confusables: because of + NP; if + finite clause
evidence_note: Free supplementive phrase, not a finite linker.

target_pattern: Compared with + noun phrase, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: frames the main statement against a comparison baseline
confusables: in comparison with + NP;compared to + NP
notes: Comparison baseline is active in CMP-COMPARED-WITH-TO under Module 09.

meaning_or_distinction: adds an accompanying action whose subject is explicitly supplied
confusables: V-ing free clause; with + NP + past participle
evidence_note: Useful when the non-finite subject differs from the main-clause subject.

target_pattern: With + noun + past participle, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: adds an accompanying passive state with an explicit noun subject
confusables: with + NP + V-ing; free past-participle clause
evidence_note: Use forms such as With the data verified, we released the report.

meaning_or_distinction: adds a state accompanying the main event
confusables: with + NP + V-ing; because + finite clause
evidence_note: Use when the explicit noun-state relation is meaningful.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a conventional absolute construction with its own explicit subject to mean if the weather permits
notes: Teach this conventional independent-subject chunk rather than a broad absolute-clause taxonomy.

anchor: active free V-ing requires shared subject
target_pattern: V-ing, main clause with same subject
meaning_or_distinction: keeps the understood participial subject aligned with the main-clause subject

anchor: passive free participle requires affected subject
target_pattern: Past participle phrase, main clause with affected subject
meaning_or_distinction: aligns a passive participial clause with the entity that receives the action
evidence_note: Use a clear semantic subject, not merely nearest-noun agreement.

target_pattern: V-ing, matching main clause / finite linker clause
meaning_or_distinction: rewrites when the main-clause subject cannot perform the V-ing action
confusables: V-ing free clause; when + finite clause
evidence_note: Repair may change the main subject or use a finite linker.

target_pattern: Past participle phrase, affected main subject / finite passive clause
meaning_or_distinction: rewrites when the main subject is not the entity affected by the participle
evidence_note: Keep error and repair semantically observable.

target_pattern: main clause, V-ing phrase / main clause and finite clause
meaning_or_distinction: chooses a participial supplement when the relation is clear and coordination when tense or subject must be explicit
evidence_note: Do not reduce away needed sequence, modality, or a new subject.

target_pattern: Having + past participle, main clause / After + finite clause
meaning_or_distinction: chooses a perfect participle for compact shared-subject prior action and a finite linker for an explicit subject
evidence_note: After + V-ing belongs module 05 because after heads the reduction.

target_pattern: Past participle phrase, main clause / Because + passive finite clause
meaning_or_distinction: chooses a participial passive supplement when its subject is shared and a finite clause when the causal relation needs explicitness
evidence_note: The purpose is not to treat the compact form as always superior.

meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here because linker-headed concessive reductions belong to module 05
is excluded here because linker-headed time reductions belong to module 05

target_pattern: noun + V-ing or past participle phrase
meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here because the non-finite phrase modifies a noun rather than the main clause
is excluded here because without is a preposition selecting its complement
confusables: Not + V-ing free clause; before + V-ing
evidence_note: Retain in the preposition deck, not in free non-finite clauses.

meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here because by is a preposition marking method
confusables: V-ing result clause; with + NP + V-ing

meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here when the infinitive modifies a noun rather than the main clause
confusables: the first person to arrive; purpose infinitive

target_pattern: too + adjective + to + verb / adjective + enough + to + verb
meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here because degree and result structures belong to module 09
evidence_note: Explicit scope boundary preserves a non-duplicated degree module.
notes: Route to module 09.

meaning_or_distinction: Adds two equal words, phrases, or clauses of the same functional type.
notes: Use examples at phrase and clause level without mixing unrelated grammar.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates a contrast or qualification between equal units.
notes: Contrast coordinator plus clause with subordinator and conjunctive adverb.

meaning_or_distinction: Presents alternatives at the same structural level.
notes: Use a context where the alternatives are genuinely parallel.

meaning_or_distinction: Adds a second negative independent clause and normally triggers subject-auxiliary inversion.
notes: Contrast clause-level nor with phrase-level neither...nor.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates an unexpected contrast, close to but with a stronger concessive effect.
notes: Keep both sides independent clauses.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates a result clause; unlike so that, it does not introduce a purpose clause.
notes: Bound the context so result and purpose cannot both fit.

meaning_or_distinction: In standard edited prose, a comma normally precedes a coordinator joining two independent clauses.
confusables: comma splice;no comma for shared predicate
notes: Test only clause boundary and punctuation.

target_pattern: subject + predicate X and predicate Y
meaning_or_distinction: A comma is normally omitted when one subject has two short coordinated predicates.
notes: Use a minimal pair with two independent clauses.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates three or more items; AmE commonly uses a serial comma before the final coordinator.
notes: Do not present the serial comma as the only grammatical international style.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinated noun phrases should perform the same grammatical function.
evidence_note: Generic label without one objectively gradable repair
notes: Concrete noun-phrase carriers can be added only for a demonstrated remaining error.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates two gerund clauses in the same complement or subject position.
notes: Use an anchor that licenses both only if the card clearly tests internal parallelism.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates infinitives; the second to may be shared when meaning remains clear.
notes: Back must explain when repeating to improves clarity.

meaning_or_distinction: One modal or auxiliary may govern coordinated bare infinitives.
notes: Preserve the decision visibly; author COORD-SHARED-AUXILIARY instead.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates adjective phrases describing the same referent or filling the same complement slot.
evidence_note: Generic label without one objectively gradable repair
notes: Concrete carriers remain preferable to category-label cards.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates prepositional phrases serving the same function.
evidence_note: Generic label without one objectively gradable repair
notes: Identical prepositions are not required, making a generic blank unsafe.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates clauses with comparable syntactic roles and clear shared scope.
evidence_note: Generic label without one objectively gradable repair
notes: Concrete clause carriers can be added only when one repair is uniquely motivated.

target_pattern: verb form, verb form, and verb form
meaning_or_distinction: Items in a series use consistent heads and complement shapes.
notes: Use a three-item policy or technical list.

meaning_or_distinction: A single preposition may govern coordinated noun phrases when both have the same relation.
notes: Back should note that repeating the preposition is also possible for emphasis.

meaning_or_distinction: Repeating the preposition marks two distinct relations or prevents scope ambiguity.
notes: Use a pair where repetition changes or clarifies attachment.

meaning_or_distinction: One auxiliary can take scope over two coordinated verb phrases.
notes: Use a sentence where both verbs share tense or modality.

meaning_or_distinction: Repeating an auxiliary can emphasize contrast or assign different polarity or modality.
notes: Choose a pair where repetition is meaning-bearing.

meaning_or_distinction: A repeated that may be omitted in coordinated content clauses, but repetition can prevent misparsing.
notes: Use a reporting verb that selects both clauses.

meaning_or_distinction: Emphasizes that two parallel alternatives or properties are included.
notes: Front must make both marker positions retrievable.

target_pattern: both + unit X + and + unit Y
meaning_or_distinction: Both must be placed immediately before the first of the two genuinely parallel units.
notes: Show a placement error that changes the parallel units.

target_pattern: both NP and NP + plural verb
meaning_or_distinction: A both...and compound subject normally takes plural agreement.
evidence_note: Core agreement tied to correlative frame
notes: Keep nouns singular so plural agreement is salient.

meaning_or_distinction: Presents two coordinated alternatives and places either before the first parallel unit.
notes: Use natural decision-making contexts.

target_pattern: either + unit X + or + unit Y
meaning_or_distinction: Either and or must introduce structurally parallel alternatives.
notes: Use unlike complement shapes only as the error.

meaning_or_distinction: In standard AmE, agreement with an either...or subject usually follows the nearer subject.
notes: Prefer singular/singular or plural/plural production examples; if mixed number is shown, explicitly accept recasting rather than marking every editorial alternative wrong.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates two excluded or negative alternatives.
notes: Use a context where neither is not a standalone determiner.

target_pattern: neither + unit X + nor + unit Y
meaning_or_distinction: Neither and nor must introduce structurally parallel units.
notes: Keep the semantic negatives simple.

meaning_or_distinction: In standard AmE, agreement usually follows the nearer subject in a neither...nor compound.
notes: Prefer singular/singular or plural/plural production examples; if mixed number is shown, explicitly accept recasting.

target_pattern: not only X but also Y
meaning_or_distinction: Adds a second parallel element with emphasis and requires matching scope.
notes: Use professional and conversational examples.

target_pattern: not only + unit X + but also + unit Y
meaning_or_distinction: Not only and but also must introduce the same type of structural unit.
notes: Use a clear mismatch such as a verb phrase versus noun phrase.

target_pattern: Not only + auxiliary + subject + verb, but ...
meaning_or_distinction: Clause-initial negative not only triggers subject-auxiliary inversion in its clause.
notes: The but-clause does not automatically invert.

meaning_or_distinction: Rejects one description or alternative and replaces it with a parallel one.
notes: Keep X and Y structurally matched.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates alternatives when the choice itself is embedded or left open.
notes: Route verb-selected whether clauses to Module 02; here test parallel alternatives.

meaning_or_distinction: Expresses that the result is unchanged under either possibility.
notes: Do not duplicate verb complement selection.

meaning_or_distinction: Connects the two endpoints or participants governed by between.
notes: Keep the card about and rather than the wider semantics of between.

meaning_or_distinction: Connects parallel starting and ending points on a range.
notes: Use time, quantity, and policy-range examples.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates a preferred or corrected noun-phrase alternative.
notes: Keep both alternatives as NPs.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates two activity alternatives expressed as parallel V-ing clauses.
notes: The governing frame must clearly select parallel V-ing alternatives; bare-inf and to-inf have separate rows.

target_pattern: base verb ... rather than base verb
meaning_or_distinction: After a base-form verb construction, rather than commonly coordinates a second bare infinitive.
notes: Use would or an imperative/base-form frame for closure.

meaning_or_distinction: Coordinates infinitives; repeating to is possible and may improve clarity.
notes: Do not claim that omitting the second to is mandatory.

meaning_or_distinction: Adds Y as supplementary information but does not create the same symmetric structure as and.
notes: Use word order changes to show nonsymmetry.

target_pattern: head NP as well as NP + head-controlled verb
meaning_or_distinction: A noun added parenthetically with as well as does not normally control agreement; the first head noun does.
notes: Use an unambiguous first head and avoid punctuation or proximity becoming a second test.

target_pattern: head NP along with NP + head-controlled verb
meaning_or_distinction: Along with adds a parenthetical supplement; agreement normally follows the head before it.
notes: Use an unambiguous first head and avoid punctuation or proximity becoming a second test.

target_pattern: coordinated units with repeated material when needed
meaning_or_distinction: Shared material should not be omitted when doing so creates a plausible wrong attachment or scope.
evidence_note: Generic writing principle rather than one retrievable decision
notes: Concrete preposition and auxiliary scope items already carry the useful lessons.

meaning_or_distinction: Compact legal or technical notation can mean X, Y, or both, but ordinary prose often benefits from spelling out the alternatives.
notes: The card tests the exact inclusive meaning and supplies a clearer plain-prose alternative without recommending the notation for routine production.

meaning_or_distinction: Compares one entity with a noun-phrase standard using an inflected comparative.
notes: Use adjectives that normally take -er.

meaning_or_distinction: Compares one entity with a noun-phrase standard using a periphrastic comparative.
notes: Use adjectives that strongly prefer more rather than -er.

meaning_or_distinction: Expresses a lower degree of a quality relative to a standard.
notes: Keep this card on less + adjective; the count and mass noun system is taught separately in CMP-FEWER-LESS-COUNT through CMP-LESS-MEASUREMENT.

meaning_or_distinction: Makes the comparison standard an explicit clause, often with an auxiliary.
notes: Use a context where the clause supplies a distinct subject.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses an auxiliary to stand for an understood repeated predicate in a comparison clause.
notes: Back must reconstruct the understood predicate briefly.

meaning_or_distinction: In contemporary AmE, than commonly precedes an object-form pronoun in informal and neutral use; a full subject-plus-verb comparison clause is also standard.
notes: Test a natural than me chunk and show than I am as an accepted clause alternative; do not test bare than I.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses an understood comparison clause after than with the conventional reduced form expected.
notes: Include predicted and anticipated as related examples only if natural.

meaning_or_distinction: Compares the current degree or amount with an earlier reference point.
confusables: more than before;than it was before
notes: Make the head comparative visible and retrieve than before as a unit.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a large difference before a comparative adjective or adverb.
notes: Teach that very does not normally modify a comparative.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a substantial difference in neutral or conversational English.
notes: Use advanced-topic examples without changing register.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a small difference before a comparative.
notes: Contrast small and large difference markers.

meaning_or_distinction: States the numerical size of the difference rather than the comparison standard.
notes: Use IELTS Task 1 style data but keep the structural decision closed.

meaning_or_distinction: Selects the precise as...as production frame for a multiple relative to a standard.
confusables: N times more than;by N times
notes: Do not claim every use of N times more than is ungrammatical; prefer this frame when numerical precision matters.

meaning_or_distinction: Shows that a quality or amount keeps increasing or decreasing over time.
notes: Use short comparatives such as harder and faster.

meaning_or_distinction: Shows progressive increase with an adjective that uses more.
notes: Contrast with -er and -er.

target_pattern: more efficient or faster, not more faster
meaning_or_distinction: A standard comparative normally uses either -er or more, not both.
notes: Use an adjective with an unequivocal standard comparative.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses fewer for a smaller number of countable items in careful standard English.
confusables: less + plural count noun;less than + amount
notes: Acknowledge conventional less with measurements separately.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses less for a smaller amount of an uncountable substance or abstraction.
notes: Choose clearly uncountable heads.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses less than naturally before measurements and numerical amounts, even when their units are count nouns.
evidence_note: Common standard exception to simplistic rule
notes: Use time and money examples.

meaning_or_distinction: Expresses equal degree relative to a noun-phrase standard.
notes: Make both as positions retrievable.

meaning_or_distinction: Expresses equal manner or performance relative to a standard.
notes: Choose an adverb whose form visibly differs from its adjective.

meaning_or_distinction: Expresses a lower degree without using a comparative form.
notes: State meaning relation to less...than without claiming perfect pragmatic identity.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses a finite clause as the standard for an equality comparison.
notes: Use examples such as as difficult as researchers had predicted or as quickly as conditions permit.

target_pattern: not as + adjective/adverb + as + finite clause
meaning_or_distinction: Uses a finite clause as the standard for a lower-degree comparison.
notes: Use a full subject and predicate after the second as.

meaning_or_distinction: Provides a grammatical but less common and often more formal alternative to not as...as.
notes: Do not teach it as required in ordinary AmE.

meaning_or_distinction: Expresses a twofold degree or measurement relative to a standard.
notes: Use measurable dimensions for objective interpretation.

meaning_or_distinction: Compares equal amounts of an uncountable noun.
notes: Use clearly uncountable nouns.

target_pattern: as many + plural count noun + as
meaning_or_distinction: Compares equal numbers of countable items.
notes: Use plural count nouns.

target_pattern: N times as much + mass noun + as
meaning_or_distinction: Expresses a precise multiple of an uncountable amount relative to a standard.
confusables: N times more;N times as many
notes: Use a clearly uncountable head and a measurable comparison.

target_pattern: N times as many + plural noun + as
meaning_or_distinction: Expresses a precise multiple of a count relative to a standard.
confusables: N times more;N times as much
notes: Use a plural count noun and a measurable comparison.

meaning_or_distinction: Highlights that an amount is surprisingly large.
notes: Use context that makes surprise clear and avoids equality reading.

target_pattern: as many as + number + plural noun
meaning_or_distinction: Highlights that a number is surprisingly large.
notes: Use count nouns and explicit expectation context.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks identity or equality with a comparison standard; standard English uses as, not than.
notes: Use a clear NP complement.

target_pattern: The more clause, the more clause
meaning_or_distinction: Shows that a change in one variable is associated with a change in another.
notes: Both halves should be meaningful clauses, not arbitrary slogans.

target_pattern: The more clause, the less clause
meaning_or_distinction: Shows an inverse relationship between two changing variables.
notes: Use a plausible causal or correlational context without claiming causation.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses an elliptical conventional form meaning earlier action is preferable.
notes: Teach it as an elliptical instance of the productive frame.

target_pattern: The comparative clause, the comparative clause
meaning_or_distinction: A comma conventionally separates the two halves of a correlative comparative.
notes: Only test punctuation plus recognizable frame.

meaning_or_distinction: Indicates that an excessive degree prevents or makes the infinitive outcome impractical.
notes: Ensure context supports the usual negative consequence.

meaning_or_distinction: Indicates that excessive manner or speed prevents the infinitive outcome.
notes: Use an overt verb modified by the adverb.

meaning_or_distinction: Adds the understood performer or affected participant of the infinitive with for + NP.
notes: Make the matrix subject and infinitive subject different.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks an excessive amount that prevents a following outcome.
notes: Use one bounded mass-noun context with an objective prevented consequence; do not reteach the count/mass contrast here.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks an excessive number that prevents a following outcome.
notes: Use one bounded plural-count context with an objective prevented consequence; do not duplicate the mass-noun card.

target_pattern: too + adjective + to-inf, not too + adjective + not to-inf
meaning_or_distinction: The ordinary too...to frame already carries an impossible or prevented-result implication and normally does not add not before the infinitive.
notes: Author one exact prevented-result repair such as too complex to implement; explicitly distinguish special positive frames such as too careful not to check.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks sufficient degree for the infinitive outcome; enough follows the adjective.
notes: Test word order explicitly.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks sufficient manner or performance for the infinitive outcome.
notes: Use a clearly adverbial form.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a sufficient amount or number for an outcome; enough precedes the noun.
notes: Test position relative to the noun.

meaning_or_distinction: Adds an explicit performer or affected participant to an enough...to frame.
notes: Use different matrix and infinitive subjects.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a high degree and introduces its result as a finite clause.
notes: Use a result that does not reveal a purpose reading.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks an extreme manner or degree and gives the result in a finite clause.
notes: Use a visible lexical verb and adverb.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a large number and introduces the resulting consequence.
notes: Use plural count nouns only.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a small number and introduces the resulting consequence.
notes: Use plural count nouns only.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a large amount and introduces the resulting consequence.
notes: Use uncountable nouns only.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks a small amount and introduces the resulting consequence.
notes: Avoid the adjective-size meaning of little.

target_pattern: such + a/an + adjective + singular noun + that-clause
meaning_or_distinction: Marks an extreme type or degree through a singular count noun and states the result.
confusables: so + adjective + that;such adjective a noun
notes: Test both such and article position as one construction.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses such directly before an adjective plus plural noun and introduces a result.
notes: Choose contexts that distinguish quality from quantity.

meaning_or_distinction: Uses such directly before an adjective plus mass noun and introduces a result.
notes: Choose contexts that distinguish quality from quantity.

target_pattern: so + AdjP + that-clause / such + NP + that-clause
meaning_or_distinction: So directly modifies an adjective or adverb, while such introduces a noun phrase.
notes: Use a two-sentence bounded contrast like the approved despite/although model.

meaning_or_distinction: In formal analytical writing, such can be predicative and introduce a clause describing the resulting or defining condition.
notes: Use natural examples such as The constraints were such that...

target_pattern: too + AdjP + to-inf / so + AdjP + that-clause
meaning_or_distinction: Contrasts an excessive degree preventing an outcome with a degree followed by an explicit actual result.
notes: Use matched content while preserving the prevented-versus-actual distinction.

target_pattern: AdjP + enough + to-inf / too + AdjP + to-inf
meaning_or_distinction: Contrasts sufficient degree enabling an outcome with excessive degree preventing it.
notes: Use the same outcome where possible.

target_pattern: to such an extent that + clause
meaning_or_distinction: Introduces a finite result after a formal expression of extreme degree.
notes: Use sparingly and with natural academic contexts.

meaning_or_distinction: Marks an extreme degree and introduces a proposition describing the result.
confusables: to such an extent that;to the point where
notes: Use an explicit result proposition; say where may also be possible when the context is conceptualized as a stage.

meaning_or_distinction: Introduces the developed situation or stage reached after a gradual change.
notes: Use an explicit developed stage; acknowledge that may overlap in some contexts.

meaning_or_distinction: Contrasts one option, category, or framing with another parallel alternative.
notes: Use matched NP or V-ing alternatives and note routing from Module 08.

target_pattern: Compared with/to + comparison baseline, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: frames the main statement relative to an explicit comparison baseline; with is common for direct analysis and to is common for likeness, with substantial overlap
notes: Use completed comparison contexts and accepted alternatives; do not force with versus to categorically.

target_pattern: higher than + comparison standard / above + scale point
meaning_or_distinction: Higher than constructs a grammatical comparison; above locates a value relative to a threshold or point on a scale.
notes: Use an explicit two-sentence contrast; acknowledge over where the exact threshold sentence allows it.

meaning_or_distinction: The two alternatives following more and than should occupy comparable structural roles.
notes: Keep this here rather than duplicating generic parallelism in Module 08.

target_pattern: no more than / not more than + number
meaning_or_distinction: Both set an upper limit; no more than commonly adds a minimizing implication, while not more than can state a neutral formal ceiling.
notes: Use expectation-setting examples and accept the counterpart when the intended emphasis permits it.

meaning_or_distinction: Sets an upper limit without necessarily adding the minimizing emphasis of no more than.
notes: A reciprocal forced contrast would create false exclusivity.

target_pattern: no less than / not less than + number
meaning_or_distinction: Both set a lower limit; no less than commonly adds an emphatic large-amount implication, while not less than can state a neutral formal floor.
notes: Use expectation-setting examples and accept the counterpart when the intended emphasis permits it.

meaning_or_distinction: Sets a lower limit without necessarily adding the emphatic force of no less than.
notes: A reciprocal forced contrast would create false exclusivity.

target_pattern: so + adjective + as in affirmative equality
meaning_or_distinction: Affirmative so...as equality is uncommon or unacceptable in ordinary contemporary AmE; teach as...as instead.
notes: Retain to prevent an overgeneralized not so...as rule.

meaning_or_distinction: A literary or highly formal alternative to such a/an + adjective + noun that is not a priority for active IELTS-7 production.
notes: The productive such a/an + adjective + noun frame is already taught; the marked alternative is unnecessary for the deck's active-production target.

meaning_or_distinction: Speakers and technical audiences may interpret multiplicative more inconsistently, so the deck should prefer N times as...as for precise production.
notes: Active cards teach precise multiplicative alternatives; adding this wording would rehearse an interpretation risk rather than a reusable connection.

meaning_or_distinction: This is an adjective-selected preposition pattern rather than a productive comparison frame.
notes: Route the active item to Module 03.

target_pattern: prefer NP/V-ing to NP/V-ing / would rather V than V
meaning_or_distinction: The complement is selected by a lexical verb, so it belongs to Verb Patterns despite its comparative meaning.
notes: Route active contrasts to Module 02 and cross-reference Module 08 only if needed.
